content: The Founder reads the taped page from his seat without getting up. 'A public refund line on a preorder, for a brand that has Rs 1,09,900 and a painter's schedule. You know what the first comment under that will be? How do I get my money back. I'd rather handle it person to person. In DMs I can actually be generous.'

content: Head of Product stands between the table and the board. 'Two positions. Founder: case by case in DMs. CX: written and public. The report's data point, a hypothesis, is that message me didn't count as a policy for anyone. Let's hear the draft, then the cost, then the wording.'

content: Research is already sketching it: two waitlist pages, identical except one carries a refund-or-replacement line. Same reel, split traffic, count signups. For once the cheapest test in the room is also the one that answers the founder's fear directly.

content: Brand squints at the draft. 'If this has to exist, it can't sound like an airline. One short paragraph, our voice, on the bio link. Not a terms page nobody reads.'

content: Growth surprises everyone by siding with CX. 'Honestly? A clear remedy line is a conversion asset. Skeptics in that report were doing refund maths in the comments. Give them the answer before they ask.'

content: Community speaks gently but doesn't back off. 'Being generous in DMs only helps the people brave enough to DM a faceless account. Everyone else just reads the silence.'

content: CX reads the draft aloud, slowly. 'Proposal, not policy. One: if your seed doesn't sprout within the guide's window, send a photo and we send a replacement seed. Two: if your order isn't dispatched by the date we gave you, you can choose a full refund. Three: if your unit arrives damaged, photo and we replace or refund. That's it. Three promises, public, on the link.'

proposals.text: Three-line public remedy promise: (1) replacement seed if no sprout within the guide window, with photo; (2) full refund option if not dispatched by the stated date; (3) replace or refund for damage on arrival, with photo
proposals.cost: (1) low; (2) and (3) exposure modelled by Finance
proposals.test: waitlist A/B with vs without the remedy line

content: Ops points at line two with their pen. 'Line two ties a refund to my dispatch date. I can't give you a date until the painting is timed. If you print that before I know, you've written a refund cheque against my guess.'
round_time: After lunch, Day 1 - Pain point 2: no refund or replacement policy

content: Finance puts the calculator down hard. 'Line one I can live with, it's a seed and postage. Line two is the problem. Preorder cash goes into sourcing and paint before anything ships. If dispatch slips and even a chunk of buyers take a full refund, I'm repaying Rs 1,099 each with money that's already been turned into tins. The worst case is the whole Rs 1,09,900. I want a cap or replacement-first, not refund-first.'
round_time: After lunch, Day 1 - Pain point 2: no refund or replacement policy

proposals.text: Finance counter-proposal: replacement-first for seed and damage; refund only for non-dispatch, with exposure capped by not taking more preorders than can be dispatched in the window
proposals.cost: limits worst case below Rs 1,09,900 gross
proposals.test: track refunds requested vs dispatch delays

disagreement: Finance (cap, replacement-first) vs CX (refund option for non-dispatch)

content: Legal's tile unmutes. 'Two cautions. First, whatever the policy is, consumer-protection rules may already give buyers rights that our wording can't take away. Verify with a professional before anyone writes replacement only. Second, a refund tied to a date only works if the date is real. That's Ops's point, and it's a legal one too.'
round_time: After lunch, Day 1 - Pain point 2: no refund or replacement policy
